effective_from_basis: The validity window of THIS ENCODING. Adding a jurisdiction, or flipping one to clock_rules_available: true, means a new rule_version with a later effective_from -- not an edit in place -- so that a due date (or a recorded absence of one) stays explainable afterwards. REGISTER-SHAPES-V0.md 5.3.

governing_rule.statement: V0 implements clock rules for US (21 CFR 803) and EU (MDR Art. 87) only, because those are the two regimes the reference actually verified. For any other jurisdiction, clock_rules_available = false and the product shows NO due date and says why.
governing_rule.why: A product that shows no due date and says why is telling the truth; one that invents a TGA deadline is not. An absent due date with a stated reason is a better demo than a fabricated deadline.

availability_test.statement: clock_rules_available is true only when BOTH conditions hold.
conditions: A rule set file exists in reference-data/clock-rules/ for this jurisdiction's applicable regulation.
A public-holiday calendar exists in reference-data/holidays/ for this jurisdiction, IF the rule set's roll-forward or work-day counting needs one.
availability_test.note: The second condition is why an EU Member State can have a fully loaded rule set and still be unavailable: MDCG 2023-3 Q14's roll-forward is national. See DE below.

jurisdictions.name: United States
jurisdictions.default_timezone_note: Several zones; the awareness timestamp supplies its own. The engine requires an explicit zone for US computations.
jurisdictions.in_scope_note: Per REGISTER-SHAPES-V0.md 10 decision 1, Asteria has a small US presence (US market entry 2026-02-09 per the generation contract). This is what unlocks the 803.3(b)(2) employee-class asymmetry.

jurisdictions.name: Australia
jurisdictions.unavailable_reason: No TGA clock rules are loaded. REGISTER-SHAPES-V0.md 5.4 scopes V0 to the two regimes the complaint-vigilance reference actually verified (US 21 CFR 803 and EU MDR Art. 87); TGA reporting timeframes were not researched and are not encoded. The product must show no due date for AU and state this reason.
jurisdictions.unavailable_reason_short: TGA clock rules not loaded in V0 -- no due date can be computed.
jurisdictions.holiday_calendar_purpose: au-vic is loaded as Asteria's OWN working calendar (internal target dates, meeting scheduling, who was in the office). Its presence must not be read as regulatory clock support. A loaded calendar is a necessary, not a sufficient, condition -- see availability_test.

jurisdictions.name: Germany
jurisdictions.unavailable_reason: The MDR Art. 87 rule set IS loaded and applies here, but no German public-holiday calendar is loaded. MDCG 2023-3 Q14's roll-forward is national -- the complaint-vigilance reference states plainly that the due date for the same event differs between Germany and Ireland -- so without a German calendar there is no honest due date, only a plausible one. Load a DE calendar and this flips to true with no rule-set work.
jurisdictions.unavailable_reason_short: MDR rules loaded, but no German public-holiday calendar -- the Q14 roll-forward is national.
jurisdictions.why_listed: Listed to make the availability_test visible: a jurisdiction can have a complete, verified rule set and still be unavailable. It is the cheapest demonstration that clock_rules_available is a data question, not a regime question.

fallback_for_unlisted.unavailable_reason: This jurisdiction is not in the V0 jurisdiction enum. No clock rules are loaded for it and none may be inferred.
fallback_for_unlisted.unavailable_reason_short: Jurisdiction not supported in V0 -- no clock rules loaded.
fallback_for_unlisted.statement: Any jurisdiction code not listed above resolves to this entry. There is no default rule set and no nearest-neighbour guess: an unlisted jurisdiction NEVER receives a computed due date.

register_mapping.note: How this file lands on the register.
register_mapping.ui_contract: When clock_rules_available is false, render unavailable_reason_short next to the empty due date. Never render a blank due date with no explanation, and never substitute an internal target date for a statutory one (REGISTER-SHAPES-V0.md 2.6: internal_target_due is a separate field for exactly this reason).
